lifecycle_corrections.finalizer_exceptions: The finalizer is exception safe: every stream, log, hash and removal step is recorded on its own and the process reaper always runs. The root is removed only after a proven cleanup and the removal is verified instead of ignored; any ordinary failure keeps the root, keeps the reservations and cannot retain exit 0.
lifecycle_corrections.global_wall_accounting: The global actual wall is accounted once by the idempotent settlement of the session. The child records keep their own observed lifetime under a truthful label.
lifecycle_corrections.reaper_custody: At the finalizer revoke the live original handles are terminated and killed with a bounded cleanup that is clipped to the remaining child budget and to the session deadline, before the final wait. An unproven child keeps its occupied charge, keeps the root and keeps the watchdog armed.
lifecycle_corrections.settlement_wiring: The real finalization settles the session exactly once after the cleanup work and captures the session evidence after the settlement, so the global actual wall of the run reaches the shared counter. An ordinary settlement or counter failure retains the root and yields a nonzero receipt, and the settlement never releases an unknown charge.
lifecycle_corrections.termination_deadline: One absolute stop deadline per child: min(child started + per_process_seconds, session cleanup deadline). The remaining time is recomputed before every wait, the post kill wait included, so the total stop never exceeds the ten second child budget even when both waits time out.
lifecycle_corrections.unknown_watchdog: An unknown live handle stays eligible for the bounded safety action: the watchdog acts on STARTED and on UNKNOWN handles, the charge keeps its slot, the root is retained and the admission stays blocked. The action is bounded by a backoff window and by a declared maximum of attempts, so it is never a busy loop, and no proven cleanup is claimed for an unproven child.
lifecycle_corrections.wall_allocation: The window is derived from the actual reserved slice and the persisted session deadlines. A second runtime owner that reuses the session id is refused; the same owner is idempotent and never rebases the window.

rules: The executor never creates, resets or truncates the counter.
A missing counter is a refusal, never an empty budget.
Every start is charged atomically under an exclusive file lock BEFORE the operating system action; the charge is PENDING until the original handle has been taken and then STARTED.
A charge is never removed and never refunded; an unknown start keeps its reservation and keeps its concurrency slot.
PENDING, STARTED and UNKNOWN all occupy a concurrency slot; only STOPPED and TIMED_OUT release it.
The settlement of a charge happens exactly once; a repeated settlement can neither free an unknown charge nor charge the budget twice.
A child keeps its own observed lifetime on its record; the global actual wall is accounted once by the settlement of the session and is never the sum of the child ages.
The session wall is the actual session span including the cleanup, not the sum of the child ages at a late reap.
The window is bounded by the ACTUAL reserved slice: a reservation of 60 seconds gives at most 30 seconds of admission and 30 seconds of cleanup, never the remaining pool of 180.

The reservation, its start and its deadlines are persisted by the shared counter; the same runtime owner is idempotent and never rebases the window, and a different runtime owner that reuses the same session id is refused.
The summed reservations stay at or below the shared pool and are never refunded; a rebind never refills the pool.
A shared pool at 179 seconds refuses a new start before the operating system action even when the local clock of a fresh executor starts at zero.
The counter identity is the budget_id that the root seals; a foreign identity is refused.
The shared count spans invocations and candidate rebinds; it never resets.
